# windows_local_users (Data Source)

Reads the local user inventory of the remote Windows host without managing it. This is a **sibling collection** of `windows_local_user` — every `users` element carries the same attributes as the singular data source, plus `is_builtin`.

Optional filters narrow the result: `name_regex` (RE2 match on the SAM account name), `enabled` (keep only enabled or only disabled accounts) and `include_builtin` (drop built-in accounts such as Administrator and Guest). Omitted filters match everything.

`users` carries one object per matching account, sorted by name (case-insensitive); `names` and `sids` carry the same accounts in the same order. An empty match is a valid empty list, never an error.

The Terraform data source ID is a query-ID: the hex SHA-256 of the normalised filter set.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Every enabled local user account on the target host.
data "windows_local_users" "enabled" {
  enabled = true
}

output "enabled_user_names" {
  value       = data.windows_local_users.enabled.names
  description = "SAM account names of every enabled local user on the host."
}

check "no_unexpected_admins" {
  assert {
    condition     = alltrue([for u in data.windows_local_users.enabled.users : u.is_builtin || startswith(u.name, "svc-")])
    error_message = "Unexpected enabled local user found; review the account inventory."
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Restrict the result to enabled (true) or disabled (false) accounts. Omit (null) to match every account.
- `include_builtin` (Boolean) Whether to include built-in accounts (SID RID below 1000, e.g. Administrator, Guest). Omit (null) means true.
- `name_regex` (String) Restrict the result to users whose SAM account name matches this RE2 regular expression (case-sensitive; prefix the pattern with (?i) for a case-insensitive match).
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Data source ID (query-ID); hex SHA-256 of the normalised filter set (raw regex, enabled tri-state, include_builtin).
- `names` (List of String) SAM account names of the matching users, in the same order as users. Empty when no user matches the filters.
- `sids` (List of String) SIDs of the matching users, in the same order as users. Empty when no user matches the filters.
- `users` (Attributes List) Matching local users, sorted by name (case-insensitive). Empty when no user matches the filters. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--users))

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--users"></a>
### Nested Schema for `users`

Read-Only:

- `account_expires` (String) RFC3339 timestamp of the account expiry date, or empty string when the account never expires.
- `account_never_expires` (Boolean) True when the account has no expiry date set.
- `description` (String) Free-text description of the user account.
- `enabled` (Boolean) True when the account is active and not disabled.
- `full_name` (String) Display name of the user account.
- `is_builtin` (Boolean) True when the account is a built-in account (SID RID below 1000, e.g. Administrator, Guest).
- `last_logon` (String) RFC3339 timestamp of the last logon, or empty string if the account has never been used.
- `name` (String) SAM account name of the user.
- `password_last_set` (String) RFC3339 timestamp of the last password change, or empty string if not yet set.
- `password_never_expires` (Boolean) True when the account password has no expiry policy.
- `principal_source` (String) Origin of the account: Local, ActiveDirectory, AzureAD, MicrosoftAccount, or Unknown.
- `sid` (String) Security Identifier of the user.
- `user_may_not_change_password` (Boolean) True when self-service password change is blocked for this account.
